title: Cops Trapped in Real-Life Horror Movie
description:
MIDWEST SAFETY: Uncover. Inform. Empower.

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

MERCH! Midwest-Safety.com

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Tips? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

This suspect, Mark Ferriolo, a 23-year-old male and his wife, Ruth Patton, a 42-year-old female, who was the woman heard interfering with the incident, were both arrested that night. Reports indicate Mark has both eluded and been violent with police on multiple occasions. In an interview with Ruth, she stated that while her and Mark were driving prior to the incident, they saw cops overseeing someone's car being towed on the side of the road. Mark thought the police were coming for them. According to Ruth, Mark wanted to quote, crash the fucking car, and both of them were going to die along with their baby, as Ruth was pregnant at the time. She also said that Mark wanted to crash into the cops and wanted to kill at least two officers that night. He then proceeded to speed by officers at approximately 80 miles an hour in a 45 mile per hour zone at the scene of the car towing and the events following unfolded. Mark was charged with two counts of first degree attempted murder of a police officer, two counts of third degree aggravated assault on a police officer, two counts of third degree alluding, four counts of fourth degree criminal mischief, and one count of fourth degree injuring a police K-9. Ruth was charged with one count of third-degree terroristic threats and one count of fourth-degree obstruction of justice for her actions during the incident. While no trial date has been set yet, both have been held without bond at the Burlington County Jail since the incident. While both the K-9 unit named Tango, as well as multiple officer-sustained injuries, none were life-threatening, and all have since fully recovered. Mark and Ruth are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law. This was the con before the storm that they probably never saw coming. And it's amazing how people could see a street full of cops but still drive like they simply don't care. Unfortunately, they found the white sedan. And I'm thinking good they found the car, at least the situations contained. But that illusion was shattered in seconds. And what actually drives a person to do this because those officers barely moved out of the way? Because this isn't just reckless, it's deliberate. And I'm thinking he must have a warrant, drugs, or a gun in the car. But he had none of that. He just wanted to crash out and hurt cops. And in a similar situation in Bismarck, North Dakota, in March of 2014, an officer was severely injured after being intentionally hit by a car that was occupied by a female suspect. Now, thankfully, the officer did survive, but I can't say the same for the suspect. In 2024, 49 officers were murdered by gunfire, but 52 were killed by vehicles, an important reminder of the real risk posed to the old survey. And I personally know an officer who lost their career and their life from a similar situation. So this was hard to watch because Mark flat out weaponized that car and almost created a homicide scene. And that street went from quiet to demolition zone. And I know those neighbors had to be terrified because your eyes probably can't believe what you're seeing. And I literally had to hold my breath when I realized he hit the canine vehicle because that hit could have been deadly. Now the officers finally did rip him out of the car and no officer was severely injured. But this guy's fuse was already lit when he sped by and I'm convinced he wanted to end his life and some cops as well. And the part no one speaks about is what stays with the officers because these moments do not just disappear. They replay at night when you go to sleep long after your shift ends. And that's the part of being a cop that the public doesn't always see. And this is the way that officers carry home in their minds because they walked away from the situation but possibly emotionally scarred. But to be straight up, this was inches away from becoming a funeral process instead of an arrest. And if any officer has slipped hesitating to misjudge, this story might have ended with a badge draped in black.
